glossary.meaning: The space you're renting.
How long the lease lasts.
Your regular rent, before any extra charges.
Charges on top of your regular rent, like taxes and building costs. Missing these can count as missing rent.
The costs of running the building, like cleaning, repairs, and management.
Common Area Maintenance: the cost of shared spaces, like hallways, parking, and sidewalks.
Your part of a building-wide cost, usually based on the size of your space.
The year used as the starting point. You pay part of any increase above that year's costs.
A lease where you pay taxes, insurance, and building costs on top of rent.
Pay for someone else's losses or legal costs.
Promise not to blame someone, and to cover their losses.
Each person who signs can be made to pay the full amount, not just their share.
Handing your lease over to someone else, often when you sell your business.
Renting part or all of your space to someone else while you stay on the lease.
Something that counts as breaking the lease.
Fix a problem before the landlord can act on it.
A promise to pay if the business can't. A personal guaranty makes you, the owner, responsible.
Staying in the space after the lease ends.
Giving the space back at the end of the lease.
A form the landlord or a lender can ask you to sign confirming the lease's terms. What you sign can bind you later.
Your lease ranks below the landlord's mortgage. If the landlord loses the building to its lender, the lender may not have to keep your lease.
Your insurance company and the landlord's agree not to sue each other over covered losses.
Events no one controls, like floods or wars, that can excuse late performance.
Even though. This clause wins over others it mentions.
The list that follows is only examples. More things are covered.
Building costs the landlord can control, like management and cleaning. Usually not taxes, insurance, utilities, or snow removal.
The landlord's right to take the space back when you ask to transfer the lease.
The new space the landlord can move you to.
A guaranty that lets the landlord collect from you without first trying the business.
A personal guaranty that ends if the business gives notice, pays through move-out, and leaves properly.
